name: Individual RCT
estimand: ATE among those randomised

name: Cluster RCT
estimand: ATE where groups are the unit of allocation
notes: Feasibility is driven by the number of clusters and the ICC, not by total participants

name: Stepped-wedge RCT
estimand: ATE averaged over exposure time
notes: Requires a phased rollout that already exists and whose order can be randomised

name: Crossover RCT
estimand: Within-person ATE
notes: Requires a reversible outcome and an adequate washout period

name: Waitlist RCT
estimand: Short-run ATE before the control group crosses over
notes: Everyone is eventually treated; the effect is identified only before crossover

name: Encouragement design
estimand: ITT of the encouragement; LATE among compliers
tier_qualifier: Tier 1 for the ITT, which inherits exchangeability from randomisation. The LATE additionally requires the exclusion restriction, which is a Tier 2 assumption.
notes: Randomises an offer or nudge rather than the treatment itself, so it suits settings where treatment cannot be withheld

name: Sharp regression discontinuity
estimand: ATE at the cutoff
notes: Requires a continuous running variable and a cutoff that is actually enforced

name: Fuzzy regression discontinuity
estimand: LATE among compliers at the cutoff
notes: Absorbs the former iv_frd entry: fuzzy RD and fuzzy-RD-as-IV are one design under two estimation framings, not two designs

name: Instrumental variables
estimand: LATE among compliers
notes: The exclusion restriction is argued on substantive grounds and cannot be tested

name: Difference-in-differences (2x2)
estimand: ATT
notes: One treatment date. Parallel trends can only be examined where more than one pre-period exists

name: Staggered-adoption difference-in-differences
estimand: Group-time ATT; aggregated to an overall ATT
notes: Kept separate from the 2x2 case because variation in treatment timing is a different data requirement. TWFE can carry negative weights here; the other estimators correct this

name: Synthetic control
estimand: ATT for the treated unit
notes: For one or a few treated units. Needs a donor pool and a long pre-period; the augmented estimator is the fallback where pre-period fit is poor

name: Controlled interrupted time series
estimand: Change in level and slope relative to a control series
estimator_options: Segmented regression with control series|Comparative ITS
notes: The control series is what lifts this above a single series. Placed at Tier 3 by sign-off rather than Tier 2

name: Regression discontinuity in time
estimand: Effect at the date of the policy change
notes: Placed at Tier 3 by sign-off: continuity across a date is a time-series claim that nothing else changed, not local randomisation

name: Matching
estimand: ATT or ATE on the region of common support
estimator_options: Propensity score matching|Mahalanobis matching|Coarsened exact matching
tier_qualifier: Upper Tier 4 where prior outcomes are matched on and comparability is demonstrated rather than asserted
notes: Blocks on covariate richness. Balance diagnostics are the characteristic check

name: Weighting
estimand: ATE or ATT
notes: Kept separate from matching because it blocks on positivity rather than covariate richness, and extreme weights are its characteristic failure mode

name: G-computation and standardisation
estimand: ATE or ATT
notes: Models the outcome rather than treatment assignment, so model specification rather than balance is the diagnostic

name: G-methods for time-varying treatment
estimand: Effect of a treatment strategy sustained over time
notes: For confounders that are themselves affected by prior treatment, where conventional adjustment is biased in both directions

name: Interrupted time series
estimand: Change in level and slope at the interruption
notes: No comparison group, so the verdict rests entirely on the pre-intervention trend having continued. Segmented regression is the usual estimator, not a separate design

name: Contribution analysis
estimand: Confidence in a stated contribution claim
notes: Builds a structured causal narrative; requires no counterfactual

name: Realist evaluation
estimand: Context-mechanism-outcome configurations
notes: Requires stakeholder access to elicit mechanisms

name: Process tracing
estimand: Confidence in a hypothesised causal pathway
notes: Requires documentary or interview evidence at each step of the pathway
